findings.title: Cache key uses Python's randomized hash(), making the cache unstable and collision-prone
findings.body: The cache key is built with `hash(tuple(sorted(project_ids)))`. Python's `hash()` for tuples of ints is deterministic per-process but string/salted hashing and, more importantly, inter-process agreement is not guaranteed across versions/configurations; worse, collisions on the truncated hash mean two different project sets can share one cache entry and get the wrong upsampling decision. The invalidation helper (`invalidate_upsampling_cache`) computes the key the same way, so a key produced in one worker can be unreachable from another. Use a stable, explicit representation (e.g. sorted ids joined by ",", or a md5/sha of it).

findings.title: 60s caching of allowlist eligibility silently serves stale upsampling decisions
findings.body: `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` caches the allowlist eligibility for 60 seconds keyed by org+project set. Because the result drives whether `count()` is replaced by `sum(sample_weight)`, a stale cache entry means the same query returns counts off by the sample-rate factor (e.g. 10x) for up to a minute after an allowlist change, and users will see charts flip between upsampled and raw values. There is no invalidation hook wired to the option change (the provided `invalidate_upsampling_cache` is never called anywhere in this PR). The option lookup is already an in-memory/cached option read, so the added cache gives little benefit for a real correctness risk; consider dropping it or wiring invalidation to the option update signal.

findings.title: Naive substring match treats negated error queries as error-focused
findings.body: `_is_error_focused_query` returns True whenever the lowercased query string contains `event.type:error`. Queries like `!event.type:error`, `event.type:error OR event.type:transaction`, or a message search containing that literal text will be classified as error-only, so `count()` is rewritten to `sum(sample_weight)` over rows that include transactions (where `sample_weight` is absent/0), producing wrong counts. Parse the query (or require the dataset to be `errors`) rather than substring matching.

findings.title: Allowlist membership test is O(n*m) on a list
findings.body: `allowlist` comes from `options.get(...)` as a list and is then used with `project_id in allowlist` for every project. For large allowlists and multi-project queries this is quadratic on a hot API path. Convert to a `set` once before the `all(...)` check.

findings.title: Unused `organization` parameter in _are_all_projects_error_upsampled
findings.body: `_are_all_projects_error_upsampled(project_ids, organization)` never uses `organization`; the allowlist is purely project-id based. The parameter misleads callers into thinking the check is org-scoped (it isn't, so project ids from other orgs would pass). Either remove it or validate project ownership.

findings.title: Accidental git submodule 'sentry-repo' committed
findings.body: A gitlink entry `sentry-repo` pointing at commit a5d2909 was added, with no corresponding `.gitmodules` entry. This will break `git submodule` operations and clones/CI for anyone checking out the branch. It is unrelated to the feature and should be removed.

findings.title: Test factory derives sample_rate from error_sampling context, diverging from production ingestion
findings.body: `_set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling` injects `normalized_data["sample_rate"]` from `contexts.error_sampling.client_sample_rate` only inside the test factory. If production relay/event-manager does not do the same, the new snuba tests (asserting count == 10 for a 0.1 sample rate) will pass while the real pipeline never populates `sample_weight`, giving false confidence. The derivation belongs in the real normalization path, or the tests should assert against data produced the production way.

findings.title: Bare `except Exception: pass` hides malformed sample-rate data
findings.body: Both try/except blocks swallow all exceptions silently. A non-numeric or malformed `client_sample_rate` will silently leave `sample_rate` unset, so an upsampling test would fail with a confusing count mismatch rather than the real cause. Narrow to `(TypeError, ValueError, AttributeError)` and/or avoid the try entirely by using `.get()` chains on known dict types.

findings.title: New `upsampled_count` function is publicly exposed in discover
findings.body: `SnQLFunction("upsampled_count", ...)` is registered without `private=True`, unlike the neighbouring internal functions. That means any API consumer can request `upsampled_count()` on any project, bypassing the allowlist gating in `error_upsampling.py` and getting `sum(sample_weight)` values for non-upsampled projects (where sample_weight may be null/0, producing misleading numbers). Mark it private if it is only meant to be injected by the server-side transform.

findings.title: upsampled_count declares default_result_type "number" while returning Int64
findings.body: The aggregate is wrapped in `toInt64` but `default_result_type` is `"number"` rather than `"integer"` as used by the other count functions. The response meta will advertise a float-ish type for an integer count, which can affect client formatting/axis rendering.

findings.title: No test covers the new caching path; cached values can leak between tests
findings.body: The unit tests only exercise the private helpers (`_are_all_projects_error_upsampled`, `_is_error_focused_query`, `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform`) and never call `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects`, so the newly added cache read/write and `invalidate_upsampling_cache` are untested. The endpoint tests in test_organization_events_stats.py mock `options` but do not clear the cache between tests; since the cache key only depends on org id + project ids, an entry written by `test_error_upsampling_with_allowlisted_projects` can make a later test with a different mocked allowlist return the stale eligibility, producing order-dependent flakes.

findings.title: Upsampling eligibility recomputed on every _get_event_stats invocation
findings.body: `_get_event_stats` is called up to four times per request by the dashboard-split logic, and each call re-runs `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` (option read + cache get/set). The comment claims the result is cached for consistency, but nothing is memoized per-request. Compute it once outside the closure (it depends only on snuba_params/organization/dataset/request) to avoid repeated work and guarantee a consistent decision across the split queries.

findings.title: Column transform duplicated in three branches instead of once
findings.body: `if upsampling_enabled: final_columns = transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling(query_columns)` is repeated in the top-events, rpc, and default branches. Besides the duplication, the upsampling decision is computed from the outer `dataset` while the query may actually run against `split_dataset`/`discover` passed in as `scoped_dataset` (see get_event_stats_factory), so an errors-dataset decision can be applied to a discover query and vice versa. Pass `scoped_dataset` to the eligibility check and transform once.
